chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ibn Abi Nasr from Dawud ibn Sirhan said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had a debt of dirhams owed to him by another man, so he sold [the debt] for pigs or wine while watching [the buyer], and then he was paid. He said: 'There is no objection; as for the one who receives the payment (the creditor), it is permissible, and as for the seller (of the debt), it is forbidden.'

key_terms.فَقَضَاهُ: He was paid / The debt was settled
key_terms.لِلْمَقْضِيِّ: For the one who receives the payment (creditor)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell a debt for pigs or wine in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the dual nature of selling a debt (*qard*) for non-monetary goods like pigs or wine. He distinguishes between the validity of the debt repayment for the creditor (*halal*) and the prohibition of the specific commodity or transaction method for the seller (*haram*), reflecting the Shia juristic principle that the underlying obligation remains sound even if the medium of settlement involves impure items. This highlights the nuance in *fiqh al-mu'amalat* where the purity of the debt does not necessarily transfer to the goods used for its discharge.
